definition: The price the end consumer pays at a traditional or modern market, per unit (kg, litre, item)
Market classification: traditional (morning market, night market) or modern (minimarket, supermarket, hypermarket)
The difference in price for the same commodity across regions (province/kab-kota), usually measured as a percentage of the national median
The middle value of a commodity's price distribution across all provinces on the same date; not sensitive to outliers
Daily rainfall >= 50 mm (BMKG category), assumed to be able to disrupt distribution and harvests
The role responsible for the day-to-day quality, definitions, and use of data (operational)
The role holding decision authority over data, including access, retention, and usage policy
A separate storage area for records that fail a DQ check (severity=error); these never reach silver
How recent the data is (e.g. price data no older than 30 days, weather data no older than 7 days)
A unique identifier for each ingestion pipeline run (format: timestamp-sequence), used for traceability
The raw-data layer, with a metadata envelope (_meta.source, _meta.payload_sha256, _meta.fetched_at, 90-day TTL)
The structured, validated, integrated layer (FK to ref), ready for analytics and dbt modeling
The analytics-mart layer (dimensional model: dim/fct/mart) produced by dbt transforms, for BI and reporting
A table mapping region codes between sources (BPS, Bapanas, WFP, BMKG) so data can be joined
Harga Eceran Tinggi (ceiling retail price) - the highest observed price indicator for a commodity in a given region and period
The technical role managing storage infrastructure, backups, security, and physical data access
The role that uses data for analysis, reporting, or decision-making (BI, data scientist)
